title: Beautiful Move: The Rook Offer
summary: Offer the rook with check, then exploit either king capture or queen capture with a precise queen maneuver.

nodes.question: How can White break the mutual defenses?
nodes.explanation: The physical demonstration starts with White Kf1, Qa2 and Rb1 against Kh1, Qa8 and Rg8. Kf2 opens the rook’s first-rank line while shielding h2 from Qa2.

branches.title: The king captures the rook
commentary: The physical demonstration starts with White Kf1, Qa2 and Rb1 against Kh1, Qa8 and Rg8. Kf2 opens the rook’s first-rank line while shielding h2 from Qa2.
Kf2+ discovers check from Rb1 along the first rank as Kf1 leaves it. It also protects the queen’s eventual g2/g3 mating squares.
Kh2 escapes the discovered rook check, but White’s king on f2 controls g1/g2/g3.
Rh1+ offers the rook next to the black king. White uses a forcing sacrifice to break the position open.
Kxh1 accepts with the king. Black has moved off h2 and gives White a new checking angle.
Qb1+ checks across the first rank and forces the black king upward again.
Kh2 is forced because White’s king controls g1/g2.
Qh7# checks down the h-file. Kf2 covers g1/g2/g3 and Qh7 covers h1/h3, leaving no flight or interposition.
branches.explanation: Qh7# checks down the h-file. Kf2 covers g1/g2/g3 and Qh7 covers h1/h3, leaving no flight or interposition.

branches.title: The queen captures the rook
commentary: The physical demonstration starts with White Kf1, Qa2 and Rb1 against Kh1, Qa8 and Rg8. Kf2 opens the rook’s first-rank line while shielding h2 from Qa2.
Kf2+ discovers the rook check along the first rank.
Kh2 moves away from the line while staying near the white king.
Rh1+ sacrifices the rook and forces Black to choose a capturer.
Qxh1 uses the queen to capture. Black keeps the king on h2 but abandons Rg8.
Qxg8 removes the black rook. White has created a zugzwang arrangement with a mating threat on g2.
Kh3 is the illustrated king move, leaving the h2 shelter.
Qg3# mates next to the king, protected by Kf2. The black queen on h1 cannot capture g3.
branches.explanation: Qg3# mates next to the king, protected by Kf2. The black queen on h1 cannot capture g3.

branches.title: The queen tries to keep g2 defended
commentary: The physical demonstration starts with White Kf1, Qa2 and Rb1 against Kh1, Qa8 and Rg8. Kf2 opens the rook’s first-rank line while shielding h2 from Qa2.
Kf2+ discovers check from the rook on b1.
Kh2 is the king’s forced retreat.
Rh1+ offers the rook to disrupt Black’s mutual defenses.
Qxh1 captures with the queen and leaves the black rook undefended.
Qxg8 wins the rook and threatens Qg2 mate.
Qe4 guards g2 along e4-f3-g2, trying to preserve the mating defense.
Qg1+ switches the checking angle; the queen on e4 cannot capture or interpose against this adjacent diagonal check.
Kh3 is forced, since Kf2 covers g1/g2/g3 and Qg1 controls h2.
Qg3# is protected by the white king. The black queen cannot stop this adjacent mate.
branches.explanation: Qg3# is protected by the white king. The black queen cannot stop this adjacent mate.

exercises.prompt: What does the rook sacrifice change?
exercises.answer: King capture allows Qb1+ and Qh7 mate. Queen capture abandons Rg8 and leaves White a zugzwang arrangement with two different checking angles.

startContext: The full six-piece physical setup is visually reconstructed with Kf1 (the earlier digital Pretty Sacrifice study used Ke1). The common rook-offer motif is attributed as a repeated composition pattern, not a new independent chess idea. Both captures and a selected queen defense are checked.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
